questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted non-eurocentric perspectives on literature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Waseda sent me a lot of information. The manager at my dorm was also very helpfull.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The manager was really helpfull with finding City Office. Waseda e-mailed me information as well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I didn't get a room in one of Waseda's own dorms, so they referred me to DK house.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you don't get a room in Waseda's own dorms, you will most likely live quite far away from uni (and everything else...)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I ended up moving even though I had pre-payed my stay. My dorm was very dirty and quite far away from everything.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Course registration is in September for courses that begin in October. I got very little information about course registration prior to the introduction day, and ended up registering for some courses that I couldn't drop, because I thought I had to register for the Advanced Seminars early. Their course list for exchange students wasn't updated.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There are three different periods for registration - four if you count the one only for Advanced seminars. You can't drop Advanced Seminars once you've registered for them.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They provide a guide - it is very long and slightly confusing.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very. I ended up registering for courses I wasn't aware that I couldn't drop, and because their course list wasn't updated, this turned out to be a big problem for me when I had to figure out a new schedule. Also, one of the courses I took completely changed the syllabus from what was written on the syllabus-site - but luckily they allowed me to change this one.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Wait till after the introduction day to register for anything.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some were quite easy. Most of them don't have much reading material, and the material they do have are very easy. We only read academic articles for one course. But they were interesting - they just didn't require that much.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Mandatory participation was new for me - but that was quite easy to get used to. Also, I was writing a lot of very short essays/class reports. At university of Copenhagen I usually write 2-4 longer essays per semester.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Intensive Studies 9 (Survey of Japanese Literature 1)
Intensive Studies 12 (Introduction to Japanese Culture and Civilization 1)
Storytelling and Media (TCS quarter seminar)
Intensive Studies 10 (Survey of Japanese Literature 2)
Global Genre Fiction (TCS Advanced seminar)
Adaptations of Classical Japanese Literature (TCS quarter seminar)
Intensive Studies 15 (Introduction to Japanese Thought and Religion 1) 
Intensive Studies 24 (European Thought 2)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Any course by Takai Shiho. I also really enjoyed Intensive Studies 15 (Introduction to Japanese Thought and Religion 1) .

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The people in the clubs are mostly Japanese students (unless you go to the international one) and they don't speak english too well. This is a me-problem tho - I don't speak Japanese.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Clubs / circles, festivals

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't really go to any so I wouldn't know.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Traveling out of Tokyo. I really enjoyed Kanazawa.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The language barrier is always going to be a problem - but it becomes way easier over time. And people are so nice. Just do what everybody else is doing and you'll be fine.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Mostly just the language thing - but again, that is a me-problem.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very, very, very nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't stress too much about not hearing anything from Waseda - they send out information quite late, but they will send it.
If you can't get a room in Waseda's own dorms, find a dorm yourself.
Be prepared to spend some time at City Office (and if you don't speak Japanese, have google translate ready), and remember to tell them that you are a student when you're setting up insurance.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Other exchange students probably have the same problems as you - so just ask them. It's easier to figure stuff out as a group.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Language barrier. The dorm.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
